newsitem.title: BELGIUM: Belgian bond business seen picking up only slowly.
newsitem.headline: Belgian bond business seen picking up only slowly.

text.p: Business in Belgian linear bonds, which edged up in thin dealings on Friday on the back of unexpectedly low U.S. November durable goods orders, is seen picking up slowly next week with the New Year break intervening.
"It went up a bit on the back of the U.S. durable goods figures, but there was not much business," one trader said.
"It will pick up a bit next week, but only very slowly," he added.
New orders for all types of U.S. durable goods fell 1.6 percent in November -- the first decline in three months and completely counter to analysts' expectations.
The yield of the benchmark 2006 OLO was 5.88 percent against Tuesday's closing 5.90, with the spread over German Bunds nine basis points against Tuesday's 10.
The March futures contract rose 27 basis points to a day's high of 120.27 in a late flurry of business just before the market closed.
